Each method turns form input into service arguments (for example, parsing a string with new Date(form.startsAt)), hands the call to SchedulingService or VisitNotesService in the business layer, and shapes the result for output, either through present() or with a small { count } response. The file holds no business rules: no booking checks, overlap detection or cancellation policy. It does no persistence and holds no other infrastructure logic. Passing new Date() as the cancellation time just supplies the current time to the service and makes no decision of its own. Counting the notes in addNote only builds the response from data the service returns.
